import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Prepare the plot
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatter plot (bubble chart)
# We visualize the relationship between price and megapixels,
# with bubble size representing camera weight and color representing sensor type.
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(30, 1000),  # Control the range of bubble sizes
    alpha=0.7,
    palette='viridis',
    ax=ax,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5
)

# --- Customization for clarity and insight ---

# Set plot title and axis labels
ax.set_title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels, Sized by Weight and Colored by Sensor Type', fontsize=18, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)

# Format the y-axis to show dollar signs and commas
formatter = FuncFormatter(lambda x, pos: f'${x:,.0f}')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Adjust tick label sizes
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=10)

# Improve legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the hue and size legends
hue_legend_labels = df['sensor_type'].unique()
size_legend_handles = handles[len(hue_legend_labels)+1:]
size_legend_labels = labels[len(hue_legend_labels)+1:]

# Create a new legend for hue (Sensor Type)
hue_legend = ax.legend(
    handles[:len(hue_legend_labels)],
    labels[:len(hue_legend_labels)],
    title='Sensor Type',
    title_fontsize='12',
    fontsize='10',
    loc='upper left',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    borderaxespad=0.
)
ax.add_artist(hue_legend) # Add the first legend back to the plot

# Create a new legend for size (Weight)
size_legend = ax.legend(
    size_legend_handles,
    size_legend_labels,
    title='Weight (grams)',
    title_fontsize='12',
    fontsize='10',
    loc='upper left',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6),
    borderaxespad=0.
)


# Add an annotation for an interesting cluster
# Find a representative point for Full Frame cameras
full_frame_cluster = df[df['sensor_type'] == 'Full Frame'].sort_values('price_usd', ascending=False).iloc[5]
ax.annotate(
    'High-end Full Frame cameras:\nHigh price, megapixels, and weight',
    xy=(full_frame_cluster['megapixels'], full_frame_cluster['price_usd']),
    xytext=(40, 5500),
    arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', arrowstyle='->', connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.1"),
    fontsize=10,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="aliceblue", ec="grey", lw=1, alpha=0.9)
)


# Set plot limits to provide some padding
ax.set_xlim(df['megapixels'].min() - 5, df['megapixels'].max() + 5)
ax.set_ylim(0, df['price_usd'].max() * 1.05)


# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Make space for the legend on the right

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)
